sentences.text: This predator featured a compact, tall, and broad cranium built to withstand twisting stresses while capturing prey.
The biggest known individuals of S. vorax measured about 4.6 meters long, estimated using body proportions similar to Liopleurodon.
However, some researchers propose the animal might have grown to over 10 meters in total length.
Andrews first named this genus in 1909.
The defining specimen is a flattened skeleton recovered from the Callovian Oxford Clay of England.
Most experts agree it mainly ate belemnites, soft-bodied cephalopods, and ammonites.
Specialized salt-excreting organs likely helped it regulate fluids while drinking ocean water.
New analyses suggest its body structure for swimming differed significantly from modern animals in similar roles.
Taxonomists place Simolestes within the family Rhomaleosauridae.
This extinct group of pliosauroids inhabited waters in present-day England and India.
They roamed from the Bajocian to the Tithonian stages, roughly 168.6 to 143.1 million years ago.
A species from the Tithonian Bhuj Formation of India is tentatively linked to Simolestes, but this assignment is viewed with skepticism.
